finding.claim: Stored SSRF: the user-supplied callbackUrl is stored without validation and later requested by the server every minute, so any client can make the server POST to internal or arbitrary hosts such as cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, localhost, or internal services.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send with HttpRequest built from URI.create(cb) (Jobs.java:20-24)

trace.note: stored in subscriptions map with no scheme, host or IP validation
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored value
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, or DNS resolution check on the path. HttpClient.newHttpClient() follows no redirects by default (NEVER policy), but this does not restrict the initial target. The response body is discarded, so this is mostly blind SSRF, though the POST side effects and internal port or host probing via timing and errors still apply.

verdict.reason: Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and Jobs.java:19-24 builds URI.create(cb) and POSTs to it with no allowlist, scheme or IP checks (the only regex guard at line 30 protects thumb(), not this path); no auth is visible, and the response body is discarded, so the SSRF is blind.
